KEMA reopens FY27 Grant-in-Aid application period through Oct. 30

LĪHUʻE – The Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency (KEMA) has reopened the application period for its Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Grant-in-Aid program, starting today, Oct. 16. The new deadline is Friday, Oct. 30.

New applicants are encouraged to apply. Organizations that have already submitted an application may submit an updated one if they choose. Previously submitted applications will remain in the applicant pool unless an updated application is submitted in its place.

The program is intended to benefit the people of the County of Kauaʻi by funding community emergency preparedness needs for which adequate federal or state funding cannot be secured. Proposals will be reviewed and considered for funding.

Funding is available through four opportunities across the following categories. Use the links below to download each application:

- Establishing and administering new Community Emergency Response Teams, or CERT (two separate funding opportunities, up to $10,000 each)
CERT Startup Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/cert-startup-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf

- Providing aerial support for damage assessment, search and rescue, and public warning and notification (up to $10,000)
Emergency Management Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/em-support-fy26-27-update-oct-2026.pdf

- Supporting sheltering operations as part of Emergency Support Function 6 (ESF-6): Mass Care and Human Services (up to $50,000)
Shelter Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/shelter-support-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf

Eligible applicants include private and nonprofit organizations. Applications are also available at www.kauai.gov/KEMA under the Announcements section.

Proposals must be received on or before 4:30 p.m. HST on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. This is a received-by deadline, not a postmark date. Proposals received after the deadline will not be considered and will be returned to the applicant.

Applicants will be notified of funding decisions on or around Nov. 13, 2026. The project funding period will run from Nov. 20, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

2026-10-17T00:03:15 [water]
*Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026*

LĪHUʻE - On Thursday, September 24, 2026, the Board of Water Supply, County of Kauaՙi, formally adopted amendments to the following sections of Part 4 of the Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water (DOW), County of Kauaՙi, for Fixing Rates for the Furnishing of Water Service in the County of Kauaՙi:

*_Section I. General Use Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section III. Agricultural Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section V. Private Fire Service Charges_* – Section revised to change wording to correspond with amended Use Charge.

The increase in service charge and use charge rates goes into effect on November 1, 2026. Customers can expect to begin seeing the updated rates on billing statements starting *December 1, 2026. *

DOW’s rates were last adjusted in 2014 and have not kept pace with the substantially rising costs of operating, maintaining, and replacing our water systems.  These adjustments align with those of other water utilities and, along with the annual Consumer Price Index adjustments, will help the department keep up with the cost of services.

The Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water, County of Kauaՙi, can be found in their entirety at our website www.kauaiwater.org/about-the-board/.

For questions or concerns about your bill, please contact our Billing section at (808) 245-5442, or email billing@kauaiwater.org. View as web page

DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15

LĪHU’E – The Department of Water (DOW) is proud to join industry leaders, businesses, community advocates, and policymakers in recognizing “Imagine a Day Without Water” (IADWW) on October 15, 2026.  This National Day of Awareness encourages Americans to reflect on the vital role water plays in every aspect of daily life and underscores how clean, reliable water sustains our families, strengthens our communities, and fuels our economy. 

From brewing morning coffee to keeping industries running, water powers everything we do. It keeps families healthy, drives local economies, and helps our communities thrive. But too often, we don’t think about it until it’s gone — when a main breaks, a drought hits, or the tap runs dry. 

*“*Access to safe, reliable water is something we can never take for granted. Very quickly, we learn how indispensable water is in our everyday lives, and how our health, environment, and economy depend on reliable access to clean water,” said Joe Tait, Manager and Chief Engineer of Kaua’i Department of Water. “Here on Kaua’i, water makes it possible for our island communities to live and have life. Investing in water means investing in our future.” 

Each year, IADWW invites us to recognize how crucial our need for water really is by visualizing life without it, just for one day. Reliable water isn’t just about convenience; it’s the foundation of public health, economic growth, and community resilience.  

According to the 2026 Value of Water Index, most Americans agree that investing in water is essential. Support for prioritizing reliable water access reached a new high, outranking all other key issues presented to voters. Voters believe continued investments in drinking water and wastewater services are critical to support life – 96% believe these water investments are critical for good public health, 95% believe it’s critical for the overall well-being of their communities, and 85% of voters believe they’re critical for a strong economy. 

For further information, please contact Tiare Nichols at 808-245-5461, or email publicrelations@kauaiwater.org.

GD-PIO NR 10-15-26 (New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach)
2026-10-16T01:58:36 [shelter]
*New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach*

WANINI – The Kauaʻi Fire Department’s Ocean Safety Bureau completed installation of a new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Thursday, Oct. 15.

“Our lifeguards are often the first line of protection for residents and visitors at our beaches,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “This tower gives them a safer place to work and a clearer view of the water at one of the North Shore’s most challenging spots. Mahalo to our Ocean Safety team for their persistence in getting this done.”

Lifeguards will now be stationed at the tower seven days a week, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The tower replaces the roving patrol the bureau has used to cover the area since the 2018 North Shore floods and landslides, which limited access beyond Hanalei and pushed more beachgoers to the beaches that remained open.

Wanini Beach is home to the “Back Channel,” an area known for strong currents and a history of drownings.

The $103,000 aluminum tower was purchased from Bausch Enterprises Inc. of Stuart, Florida. It gives lifeguards a higher vantage point to watch ocean conditions and respond to emergencies, and provides shelter from rain, wind, and sun during long shifts.

The tower was installed in-house by Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards Kleve Zarbaugh, Gerald Hurd, Tyrus Siale, Eric Pereza, Christopher Davis, and Zackery Harris, with help from Department of Public Works staff Bryson Cummings, Lance Edralin, and Brannon Rivera.

“This tower represents years of dedication, perseverance, and our commitment to protecting lives,” said Ocean Safety Bureau Chief Kalani Vierra. “Our lifeguards now have a better vantage point to monitor ocean conditions, respond to emergencies, and serve our community and visitors.”

Vierra thanked the Mayor’s Administration, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi County Council, and the North Shore community for their support.

A blessing for the tower will be held at a later date.

Beachgoers are reminded to swim near a lifeguard and check daily ocean conditions at safebeachday.com.

For more information, please contact the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

The new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15.

Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards, from left, Eric Pereza, Tyrus Siale, Zackery Harris, and Gerald Hurd at the new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15. View as web page

headline.title: New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach
headline.subject: NR 10-15-26 (New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach)

items.body:
*New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach*

WANINI – The Kauaʻi Fire Department’s Ocean Safety Bureau completed installation of a new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Thursday, Oct. 15.

“Our lifeguards are often the first line of protection for residents and visitors at our beaches,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “This tower gives them a safer place to work and a clearer view of the water at one of the North Shore’s most challenging spots. Mahalo to our Ocean Safety team for their persistence in getting this done.”

Lifeguards will now be stationed at the tower seven days a week, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The tower replaces the roving patrol the bureau has used to cover the area since the 2018 North Shore floods and landslides, which limited access beyond Hanalei and pushed more beachgoers to the beaches that remained open.

Wanini Beach is home to the “Back Channel,” an area known for strong currents and a history of drownings.

The $103,000 aluminum tower was purchased from Bausch Enterprises Inc. of Stuart, Florida. It gives lifeguards a higher vantage point to watch ocean conditions and respond to emergencies, and provides shelter from rain, wind, and sun during long shifts.

The tower was installed in-house by Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards Kleve Zarbaugh, Gerald Hurd, Tyrus Siale, Eric Pereza, Christopher Davis, and Zackery Harris, with help from Department of Public Works staff Bryson Cummings, Lance Edralin, and Brannon Rivera.

“This tower represents years of dedication, perseverance, and our commitment to protecting lives,” said Ocean Safety Bureau Chief Kalani Vierra. “Our lifeguards now have a better vantage point to monitor ocean conditions, respond to emergencies, and serve our community and visitors.”

Vierra thanked the Mayor’s Administration, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi County Council, and the North Shore community for their support.

A blessing for the tower will be held at a later date.

Beachgoers are reminded to swim near a lifeguard and check daily ocean conditions at safebeachday.com.

For more information, please contact the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

The new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15. 

Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards, from left, Eric Pereza, Tyrus Siale, Zackery Harris, and Gerald Hurd at the new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15.
